title: 1Password Pricing 2026 for Teams and Businesses
summary: 1Password pricing includes plan tier, seat count, add-ons and billing term. Calculate the total cost for your specific needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden 1Password costs and limits


The per-seat price covers only the first line of the bill. Add-ons, seat caps, tier-gated features and renewal terms each change the total, so check each against your headcount and billing term. The subsections below sort them by where they hit the bill.


### Seat counting and bundle caps


When a team outgrows the Starter Pack's seat cap, it moves to per-seat pricing and the bundle's low entry price stops applying. Guest and family-member limits work the same way: once you pass the allowance, you buy more.


**Inactive seats are also billable.** A departed contractor's still-provisioned account bills you with no user attached.


The check that catches those accounts is cheap to automate, because[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) counts a flow run as 1 credit however many steps it has.


A ten-step leaver check costs the same as the two-step shortcut it replaced, whereas per-task billing such as Zapier's charges for every step and so taxes the careful version.


### Features gated to higher tiers


If a team needs automated provisioning, it may have to move above the plan it priced, since **SSO and SCIM depend on your tier** . The Extended Access Management add-on is billed on top of the plan, which means it scales with headcount.


Three terms carry most of that decision. SSO, or single sign-on, means staff sign in to 1Password through the company's identity provider, the system that already holds their work logins, instead of with a separate password.


SCIM is the provisioning side: accounts are created and removed automatically from that identity provider, so nobody adds or deletes users by hand.


Extended Access Management is an add-on that checks and enforces security on the devices people use, which is what step 3 of the plan checklist below asks about. If you have no identity provider and no device policy, you probably need none of the three.


SCIM also bears on cost. Automated removal stops leavers occupying paid seats, so a feature that raises the tier can partly pay for itself.


Then there is integration labor, a cost the pricing page leaves out.[ContractRates.fyi](https://www.contractrates.fyi/IT-Consultant/hourly-rates) puts IT consultants at $80 per hour in the US and $75 in the UK, so a hired identity-provider setup is billed by the hour on top of the license.


Canada's figure is $25 per hour, more than three times lower. That gap may reflect the data behind the average, so treat it as a reason to get a quote, not to assume a discount.


The discount applies only to annual billing, so monthly payment costs more per seat for the same plan. The renewal price can differ from the first-term price, so check it before committing to a year.
